# readmit

`readmit` creates editable, user-owned Readmission Risk Pool (RRP)
projects. Each project includes configuration, source-mapping and
risk-provider scripts, branding, and its own Shiny application.
Persistent history can be initialized explicitly,
[`rrp_run()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_run.md)
retains completed assessments, and status and history inspection are
available.
[`rrp_refresh_products()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_refresh_products.md)
writes analytical CSVs from retained history; populated app views are a
later development stage.

## Create and open a project

After installing `readmit`, create a project at a new destination:

``` r

library(readmit)

project <- rrp_project_init(
  path = "my-rrp-project",
  project_id = "my-project"
)

rrp_project_validate(project)
```

The path is relative to your current working directory unless you supply
an absolute path. Its parent directory must already exist, and the
destination must not exist, even as an empty directory. The generated
files belong to you: edit `rrp-project.dcf`, `rrp-authoring.dcf`,
`_brand.yml`, `R/produce-canonical.R`, and `R/calculate-risk.R` for your
project.
[`rrp_project_validate()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_project_validate.md)
checks that the configuration and both authoring functions load; it does
not run them. Both generated functions begin as deliberate stubs, so the
untouched project passes this structural check. Implement the source
mapper to return the canonical discharge episodes and terminal events
described in the project README, and implement the risk provider for
eligible episodes. Validate again after editing. Validation checks that
the scripts load; it does not establish that their data or predictions
will work during a run.

Then initialize persistent history and run at an explicit UTC analytical
time:

``` r

rrp_state_init(project)
assessment <- rrp_run(
  project, as.POSIXct("2026-01-10 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)
rrp_project_status(project)
rrp_inspect_history(project, run_id = assessment$run_id)
rrp_refresh_products(project)
```

This creates empty `state/history.duckdb` tables in the project and
refuses to overwrite existing state. State initialization does not run
either authoring function. Each
[`rrp_run()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_run.md)
call obtains canonical facts, assesses eligible episodes through the
provider, and atomically appends the completed run and its episode
outcomes. It returns the run ID and accepted, failed, and ineligible
counts.
[`rrp_project_status()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_project_status.md)
also works before state initialization;
[`rrp_inspect_history()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_inspect_history.md)
requires state. Both read retained information without sourcing your
scripts. A provider failure is retained for its episode while other
eligible episodes continue. Completed runs append history; later event
knowledge does not rewrite earlier results. After at least one completed
run,
[`rrp_refresh_products()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_refresh_products.md)
reads history and writes `state/products/current-remaining-risk.csv`,
`remaining-risk-trajectory.csv`, and `operational-scope-summary.csv`. It
selects the run with the greatest analytical time, which may differ from
the most recently executed run. Supply the complete relevant discharge
population for operational assessments: a later partial run replaces the
earlier population in current products. The package determines clinical
eligibility. Eligible provider-failure episodes stay in the current-risk
file with a missing probability; earlier estimates are not substituted.
Refresh does not rerun your scripts, change history, or edit the app.
The three-file replacement is staged but is not fully atomic if a
filesystem error occurs during final replacement.

The application uses `shiny`, `bslib`, and `yaml` in the environment
where it runs. Install them there, then launch the app directly from the
same working directory used in the example:

``` r

install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "yaml"))
shiny::runApp("my-rrp-project/app")
```

The app opens with Current Risk Pool and Overview views. Its current
empty states remain until populated product views are implemented in a
later stage.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`rrp_inspect_history()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_inspect_history.md)
  : Inspect completed RRP assessments
- [`rrp_project_init()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_project_init.md)
  : Create an RRP project
- [`rrp_project_status()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_project_status.md)
  : Summarize an RRP project's retained history
- [`rrp_project_validate()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_project_validate.md)
  : Check an RRP project's authoring structure
- [`rrp_refresh_products()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_refresh_products.md)
  : Refresh an RRP project's analytical product CSVs
- [`rrp_run()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_run.md) :
  Run an RRP assessment and retain its history
- [`rrp_state_init()`](https://readmit.centralstatz.com/reference/rrp_state_init.md)
  : Initialize persistent history for an RRP project
